LESSON: SIGN READING 1.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Sign Reading 1.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 1.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: How can we tell how a story, poem or conversation will end? 2. How can we identify where events have taken place?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 1.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner articulates signs effectively as they discuss the setting and characters in a story with peers.

• Learning to Learn: The learner learns independently as they respond to direct questions by locating sentences with the answers.

Values:
Unity: Learner cooperates with peers during discussions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Learner Support Programme (peer education) as the learner guides peers in a discussion.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner applies the comprehension strategies in reading of texts in environmental activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as Hearing aids and amplifiers, pictures, signed audio-visual recordings, pocket charts, print

or digital text
